title: What the CLT says

choices: Roughly normal (bell-shaped), centered near the population mean
Roughly normal, centered near the population median
Flat (uniform), because every sample is equally likely
explanations: That's what the histogram of the delays themselves looks like.
Sample means center on the population **mean**.
Means near the population mean are far more common.

hints: The CLT is about the means, not the data.
What shape do means of large samples take?
solution: Means of large random samples are roughly normal, whatever the population's shape, and they center on the population mean.
